definitions.explanation: A character or part played by an actor in a performance, film, or play.
A function, responsibility, or official position assigned to someone in a group or organization.

examples.japanese: {主役|しゅやく}の{役|やく}をもらった。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{悪|わる}い{役|やく}ばかり{演|えん}じている。
この{映画|えいが}で{初|はじ}めて{父親|ちちおや}の{役|やく}に{挑戦|ちょうせん}した。
examples.english: In this film, I took on the role of a father for the first time.

examples.japanese: {司会|しかい}の{役|やく}を{任|まか}された。
examples.english: I was assigned the role of emcee.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}かがリーダーの{役|やく}をやらないといけない。
examples.english: Someone has to take on the role of leader.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}では{書記|しょき}の{役|やく}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: I often take on the role of note-taker at meetings.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is common in theater, film, and television contexts. Sense 2 extends to any assigned function within a group. Often combined with other words to form compounds: {主役|しゅやく} (lead role), {脇役|わきやく} (supporting role), {悪役|あくやく} (villain role), {適役|てきやく} (well-suited role).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {役|やく}を{演|えん}じる: to play a role
- {役|やく}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}ける: to take on a role
- {役|やく}に{立|た}つ: to be useful
- {役|やく}を{任|まか}される: to be assigned a role
